questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. Expert mechanics labored over the plane for three hours.

B. A small nut had fallen into a channel which prevented the gear from moving.

C. A huge plane was forced to crash land when its landing gear got stuck.

D. They were amazed when they discovered what had caused the mechanical failure.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CADB'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some grammatical or contextual connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 

 
• Sentence C is the independent sentence and talks about an incident where a plane had to crash land. 
 
• So, sentence C is the first sentence after rearrangement and mentions that the crash happened as the landing gear had gotten stuck. 
 
• Sentence A describes how the mechanics tried to correct the fault. So, the sentence "A" comes in the second position. Hence, A follows C.
 
• Sentence D which talks about the mechanics' reaction to learning what caused the mechanical failure should come after sentence A, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• Sentence B is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides further information regarding the mechanical failure. 

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is option 3 i.e. CADB.

*So, the correct paragraph is : **(******C) A huge plane was forced to crash land when its landing gear got stuck. (A) Expert mechanics labored over the plane for three hours. (D) They were amazed when they discovered what had caused the mechanical failure. (B) A small nut had fallen into a channel which prevented the gear from moving.***

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. 

Vivek should be excited / on the promotion / he’s got.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'on the promotion'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The erroneous part of the given sentence is **on the promotion.**
 
• There is an error in a **preposition **in this part. 
 
• The **preposition "on" **usually points to something specific, like a location. ** **
 
• Thus, **on **cannot be used in context of the given sentence. 
 
• This makes **option 4 **the correct answer. 
 
• The correct preposition to use here is **about **which usually means the subject of something, or something less specific.

***Correct sentence - ****Vivek should be excited / **about the promotion** / he’s got.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

She is looking after the old ladies with great affection.

options.text: The old ladies are looked after with great affection.
The old ladies were looked after with great affection.
The old ladies are being looked after with great affection.
She is looked after with great affection by the old ladies.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****The old ladies are being looked after with great affection.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **active voice.** As per the question we have to change it into** passive voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **Subject + to be (is) + present participle + Object (Active voice)**
 
• **Subject (objective case) + to be (is) + being + past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *My boss is giving many assignments. (Active voice)*
 
• *Many assignments are being given by my boss. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘she’. 
 
• The **object **of the given subject is ‘the old ladies’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• In passive voice we may omit the agent because we don't know who they are, or it's implied or unimportant, or we'd rather not say. So, we do not include **she **in the passive voice.
 
• **is looking **will be changed to **are being looked**.
 
• Correct sentence - The old ladies are being looked after with great affection.

questions.question:

• Proclaim is a verb that means to announce officially or publicly.

• Exhibit - publicly display (a work of art or item of interest) in an art gallery or museum or at a trade fair.
 
• Evince - reveal the presence of (a quality or feeling); indicate.
 
 
 
• From the above meanings, it is evident that conceal is the correct antonym for the word proclaim.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I do not / like to read / these kind / of novels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'these kind'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The erroneous part of the given sentence is "**these kind."**
 
• **"kind of novels" **is a singular phrase. 
 
• **"These" **is used with plural nouns and hence, it cannot be used before "**kind of novels". **
 
• Hence, **option 1 **is the correct answer. 
 
• To make the sentence correct we need to use **this.**

***Correct sentence - ****I do not / like to read / **this kind** / of novels.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Shall / we go / for walking / in the park?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'for walking'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of "**walking**" is incorrect instead of this we need to use **"a walk"**
 
• According to grammar, with a preposition, we always use a noun/gerund/noun phrase. "**walking**" is a present participle which is incorrect hence, we need to use a noun form of this particular verb.
 
• **'Walk' **is also used as a noun.
 
• The noun form of **'Walk' **is '**Walk'.**
 
 
• **For Example: **The **walk** along the beach at sunrise was a breathtaking experience.
 
 
 
• Let's see an example of using noun/gerund/noun phrase after a preposition.
 
 
• The food is **on the table.**
 
 

***Correct sentence - ****Shall / we go / **for a walk **/ in the park?*

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

We had to undergo __a great many difficulties.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'No improvement'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There is **no error **in the underlined part of the given sentence. 
 
• Initially, it may seem using the **indefinite article *a ***before the phrase *great many difficulties *is incorrect. 
 
• But indefinite articles often precede descriptive adjectives. - 
 
 
• **Example **- *He is a good boy. / What a nice car!*
 
 
 
• 
 
 We use** a great many + plural noun **to mean a large number of something.

 
 
• 
 
For example:

 
We had to undergo **a great many** difficulties. (We had to face a lot of problems.)

 She has** a great many **friends. (She has a lot of friends.)

 

The other options are incorrect and do not follow the rule of a great many + plural noun.

 
• Option 1) changes the order of the adjectives and makes the sentence ungrammatical.
 
• Option 2) uses a singular noun instead of a plural noun and makes the sentence ungrammatical.
 
• Option 4) omits the article a and makes the sentence unidiomatic.

 

 
• Hence, **option 3 **is the correct answer. 

***Correct sentence - ****We had to undergo **a great many difficulties.__***
